messages:
marta: quick heads-up — new model bringup (rank-3b-adapter) showed a weird MRR delta vs baseline on webqa_v2, small sample but consistent across two seeds.
liam: ugh, how big is the delta? ndcg also moved?
marta: MRR down ~2.3% at @10, ndcg@10 almost flat (+0.2%). numbers from the standard eval harness run.
zara: interesting. which candidate pool and ordering did you use? canonical vs shuffled?
marta: canonical ordering, full candidate pool ~100. I also tried topk50 only, same sign.
liam: did you compare quantized vs fp16? might be a quantization artefact.
marta: good call — fp16 (baseline) vs ptq-int8 adapter. fp16 has the expected MRR, int8 drops. but the model is an adapter-on-top checkpoint, not full fine-tune.
zara: could be adapter sensitivity to KV packing or scale shifts. any tokenization differences between offline eval and prod?
marta: tokenizer identical, preproc scripts same repo. double-checked whitespace normalization.
liam: can you paste the eval command?
marta: ```bash
# run harness
python infra/eval_runner.py --model rank-3b-adapter --weights /mnt/checkpoints/r3b-adapter.pt --dataset webqa_v2 --candidates canonical --metrics ndcg@10 mrr@10 --seed 42 --topk 100 --quant ptq-int8
```
zara: sweet. can you also run a per-query delta sweep and log to the eval tracker? want to see whether the drop is concentrated in short queries or tail.
marta: starting that now. planning: 1) per-query delta, 2) slice by query length, 3) slice by candidate doc type (passage vs doc), 4) rerun with no prefix cache to rule out KV cache mismatch.
liam: also try metric-adapter reweighting — i.e., compute a weighted ndcg that emphasizes top1-3. if ndcg flat but MRR down, it suggests more top-k position shifts.
zara: yeah, MRR is sensitive to exact rank positions. maybe re-ranking is bunching top-3. Another probe: compute top1 hit rate and mean position.
marta: added those probes. quick note: embedding distances look same distribution-wise. it's the pairwise scorer output that changed.
liam: could be score scaling (temperature). Did you normalize scores before softmax/ties?
marta: we do a simple score znorm per-candidate-set in the harness. but the new adapter model outputs narrower score spread.
zara: try a calibration layer: multiply logits by 1.1 or so and recompute mrr/ndcg as an ablation.
marta: doing a scaling sweep now: [0.8, 1.0, 1.1, 1.25]. will push results to the tracker.
liam: if scaling fixes MRR, we should add a metric-adapter step in the bringup checklist: check score variance and test small scalar calibration.
zara: agree. also add a short doc about candidate ordering sensitivity for adapters — we've seen this before with topk pruning.
marta: logging results: initial per-query delta shows that 70% of the loss comes from queries with 1–3 tokens. tail queries unaffected.
liam: aha. short queries => less context => adapter not helping priming. Could be prompt template change.
zara: can you attach the template used for concatenating query+doc? maybe the adapter expects a different separator token.
marta: template: "<Q> {query} </Q> <DOC> {doc_text} </DOC>". same as baseline. will also try running with raw concatenation (no tags).
liam: small follow-ups: 1) run adapter with fp16 to confirm quantization is the amplifier, 2) seed sweep 3 seeds, 3) sanity run with only topk20.
marta: ack. timeline: fp16 + seed sweep + scaling ablation done within 3 hrs, will post a short summary.
zara: thanks — if the fix is simple (scaling or template tweak), we can add to the onboarding playbook for adapter variants.
eval-bot: scheduled job 1764509950: eval-tracker updated with run ids rrun-9245 / rrun-9246 / rrun-9247. artifacts: per-query-deltas.csv, slice-summary.json.
marta: linking results: https://eval.internal/runs/rrun-9245 (fp16), rrun-9246 (int8), rrun-9247 (scaling sweep). main takeaway so far: fp16 MRR ~baseline, int8 drops, scaling 1.1 recovers ~60% of the gap.
liam: great — that strongly suggests a score calibration + quantization interaction. next steps: (a) add scalar calibration to quant pipeline, (b) add short-query priming test to our CI smoke, (c) update bringup checklist.
zara: I'll draft the CI test. marta, can you open a tiny PR with the scalar step and a note in onboarding doc?
marta: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
